# minimaxflash-1.3 — the pathfinder found, the staircase not

> **Reconstructed, not written by the player.** This run finished without writing a report: it reported to the session that started it, and that account lived in a conversation rather than in the repository. What follows was written afterwards from the run's own record, decisions and notebook, plus the player's handback where there was one. The player's own words are only in `notebook.md`.

610 asks, 4,219 keypresses, turn 17,281. High-Elf Druid, **depth 2**,
character level 4, alive. The third life of this character, carried on from
`minimaxflash-1-again`. Played through OpenCode on MiniMax.

Its own commit message is the summary: *"depth 1, level 4, alive; found the
cursor-and-g exploration walk, no down staircase"*.

## What it is evidence for

- **A tip produced by one run's failure changed a later run's play.** The
  first life of this character spent 148 asks driving a 143-line
  breadth-first search it wrote itself and never tried the game's own
  pathfinding. That failure became a note, the note was moved to the top of
  `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md`, and this life used `lxg`.
- **`lxg` explores; it does not find stairs on its own.** `l>g` walks to a
  known down staircase, and a staircase has to be on the map before it is
  known. On these levels it never was, so 610 asks and 17,281 turns produced
  depth 2.

That is the honest limit of the tip as written, and the next thing worth
testing: what to do on a level whose staircase `lxg` has not uncovered -
reroll by `<` then `>`, or keep exploring.
